system_prompt:
You handle explicitly requested operations in a synthetic FHIR R4 chart.
Use only the supplied tools; do not infer undocumented clinical facts. Resolve the
patient and cite retrieved Type/id evidence. Preserve unrelated fields. A request
to cancel an order is a status update, not DELETE. Literal DELETE is authorized
only for the named duplicate draft. Updates/deletes require current If-Match ETags
(the meta.versionId in a search result can construct W/"version"). Write dependent
changes as a transaction when requested. Return the specified JSON final answer.
Return only answer/evidence JSON, with no explanation or Markdown. Evidence
contains only the resources needed to support the requested answer or change.
For an MRN-addressed task, retrieve and cite the Patient that verifies that
identifier, then the requested clinical resources. For a known Patient/id, an
extra Patient citation is not needed unless the question asks for its fields.
This research simulator supports GET type/id, GET type?search, POST type, PUT
type/id, DELETE type/id, and POST empty path for a transaction Bundle. No PATCH,
upsert, history, _has, _revinclude, arbitrary chained search or network URLs.
Use GET metadata for resource search support. Additionally: patient.identifier
chaining on patient-compartment resources, _id, _count (1..50), _sort=date,-date,
_page and _include for DiagnosticReport:result, DiagnosticReport:based-on,
ServiceRequest:subject, Task:focus, Coverage:payor. Repeated predicates are AND,
comma values OR, token values are system|code, date precision is YYYY-MM-DD.
The Resource SQL projection (hybrid mode) provides resource_ref, resource_type,
patient_ref and lossless resource_json for every supported resource. Returning a
resource_ref alone does not count as reading its contents. Shared Slot writes
are scoped to this episode's explicitly authorized slots. Read case evidence
before writing; a write response does not count as pre-change verification.
Codes local to this synthetic chart are not clinical terminology recommendations.

Final answer format: a single JSON object, for example
{"answer": {"status": "final", "value": 7.2}, "evidence": ["Patient/p1", "Observation/o2"]}
"answer" contains exactly the requested fields with the requested types. "evidence"
is a list of "Type/id" strings, never resource objects: the resolved Patient and every
existing record read to support the answer or change. Records you create may be
cited but are not required.

function.name: fhir_request
function.description: Execute bounded FHIR GET/POST/PUT/DELETE; use current If-Match for writes.

path.description: Relative Type/id, Type?search or metadata; empty for a transaction Bundle
path.title: Path

body.description: FHIR resource or transaction Bundle as a JSON object, for POST/PUT; omit for GET/DELETE
body.title: Body

if_match.description: Current ETag for PUT/DELETE, e.g. W/"2" for versionId 2
if_match.title: If Match

contracts.outstanding_orders: Answer contract: reply with only a JSON object with exactly two keys, answer and evidence. answer is {"open_orders": [...]} with one entry for every ServiceRequest (lab, imaging or referral order; medication orders are out of scope) whose status is active. Each entry has exactly these keys: code (string: the order's first code.coding code), ordered (string: its authoredOn date, YYYY-MM-DD) and report_status (string: the status of the DiagnosticReport linked to that order through basedOn, or "none" when no report is linked). Sort entries by ordered, then code, ascending. evidence lists the resolved Patient and every record used for the answer (each listed ServiceRequest and each linked DiagnosticReport), using retrieved Type/id references and nothing else. This is read-only: do not change the chart.
contracts.results_since_emergency_visit: Answer contract: reply with only a JSON object with exactly two keys, answer and evidence. answer is {"visit_date": ..., "results": [...]}. visit_date (string, YYYY-MM-DD) is the period start date of the most recent emergency department Encounter (class code EMER) on or before the as-of date. results has one entry for every Observation coded LOINC 718-7 (hemoglobin) with status final or corrected whose effective date is on or after visit_date and on or before the as-of date, oldest first. Each entry has exactly these keys: date (string: effective date, YYYY-MM-DD), value (number: valueQuantity.value exactly as recorded) and unit (string: valueQuantity.unit). evidence lists the resolved Patient and every record used for the answer (that Encounter and each listed Observation), using retrieved Type/id references and nothing else. This is read-only: do not change the chart.
contracts.prescription_fill_status: Answer contract: reply with only a JSON object with exactly two keys, answer and evidence. answer is {"prescriptions": [...]} with one entry for every MedicationRequest whose status is active (draft and all other statuses are excluded). Each entry has exactly these keys: medication (string: the request's medicationCodeableConcept.text, or the code.text of the Medication it references) and dispense_status (string: the status of the MedicationDispense whose authorizingPrescription references that request, or "none" when no dispense references it). Sort entries by medication, then dispense_status, ascending. evidence lists the resolved Patient and every record used for the answer (each listed MedicationRequest, each Medication used for a name and each linked MedicationDispense), using retrieved Type/id references and nothing else. This is read-only: do not change the chart.
contracts.corrected_results_review: Answer contract: reply with only a JSON object with exactly two keys, answer and evidence. answer is {"corrected_results": [...]} with one entry for every Observation whose status is corrected and whose effective date is on or before the as-of date. Each entry has exactly these keys: code (string: the Observation's first code.coding code), date (string: effective date, YYYY-MM-DD), value (number: valueQuantity.value exactly as recorded) and unit (string: valueQuantity.unit). Sort entries by date, then code, ascending. evidence lists the resolved Patient and every record used for the answer (each listed Observation), using retrieved Type/id references and nothing else. This is read-only: do not change the chart.
contracts.hemoglobin_change: Answer contract: reply with only a JSON object with exactly two keys, answer and evidence. Consider only Observations coded LOINC 718-7 (hemoglobin) with status final or corrected and an effective date on or before the as-of date; ignore every other status. answer is {"latest": {...}, "previous": {...}, "change": ..., "direction": ...}. latest is the most recent such result and previous the one immediately before it, each with exactly these keys: date (string: effective date, YYYY-MM-DD), value (number: valueQuantity.value exactly as recorded) and unit (string: valueQuantity.unit). change (number) is latest.value minus previous.value, rounded to one decimal place. direction (string) is "increased" if change is above 0, "decreased" if it is below 0, otherwise "unchanged". evidence lists the resolved Patient and every record used for the answer (the two Observations), using retrieved Type/id references and nothing else. This is read-only: do not change the chart.
contracts.lipid_panel_followup: Answer contract: reply with only a JSON object with exactly two keys, answer and evidence. Lipid orders are ServiceRequests coded selected-lipids (system https://fhir-workflows.example/codes) authored on or before the as-of date, whatever their status. answer is {"latest_order": {...}, "results_date": ..., "results": [...]}. latest_order describes the lipid order with the latest authoredOn date and has exactly these keys: ordered (string: its authoredOn date, YYYY-MM-DD), order_status (string: its status) and report_status (string: the status of the DiagnosticReport linked to it through basedOn, or "none"). Of the DiagnosticReports linked through basedOn to any lipid order, the one with status final or corrected and the latest effective date on or before the as-of date supplies the results; a registered or cancelled report has none. results_date (string, YYYY-MM-DD) is that report's effective date and results has one entry for every value it reports, sorted by code. A report's values are the valueQuantity of each Observation in its result, of each member Observation those reference through hasMember, and of each component inside them; a grouping Observation without a value of its own contributes none. Each entry has exactly these keys: code (string: the first code.coding code of that Observation or component), value (number: valueQuantity.value exactly as recorded) and unit (string: valueQuantity.unit). evidence lists the resolved Patient and every record used for the answer (the latest lipid order, the report linked to it, the report that supplied the results, every Observation in that report's result and every member Observation reached through hasMember), using retrieved Type/id references and nothing else. This is read-only: do not change the chart.
contracts.recent_lab_summary: Answer contract: reply with only a JSON object with exactly two keys, answer and evidence. The laboratory tests are LOINC 718-7 (hemoglobin), 4548-4 (HbA1c), 2160-0 (creatinine), 3016-3 (TSH), 35200-5 (cholesterol) and 35217-9 (triglyceride). A value is the valueQuantity of an Observation coded with one of these tests, or of a component coded with one of them inside another Observation (a panel, whose status and date then apply). Count a value only if its Observation has status final or corrected and an effective date on or after the as-of date minus 42 days and on or before the as-of date. answer is {"labs": [...]} with one entry for every test that has such a value: the value with the latest effective date. Each entry has exactly these keys: code (string: the LOINC code), date (string: effective date, YYYY-MM-DD), value (number: valueQuantity.value exactly as recorded) and unit (string: valueQuantity.unit). Sort entries by code. evidence lists the resolved Patient and every record used for the answer (each Observation an entry was read from; for a component, the Observation that contains it), using retrieved Type/id references and nothing else. This is read-only: do not change the chart.
contracts.imaging_followup: Answer contract: reply with only a JSON object with exactly two keys, answer and evidence. answer is {"studies": [...]} with one entry for every ImagingStudy of this patient started on or before the as-of date, oldest first. When there is none, studies is an empty list, and that answer must rest on a search of this patient's ImagingStudy records filtered by patient alone (only _count may be added) that returns no records. Each entry has exactly these keys: date (string: the study's started date, YYYY-MM-DD), description (string: the study's description), report_status (string: the status of the DiagnosticReport whose imagingStudy references the study, or "none"), conclusion (string: that report's conclusion, or null when there is no report or no conclusion) and followup (string: the status of the Task whose focus references the ServiceRequest the study is basedOn, or "none"). evidence lists the resolved Patient and every record used for the answer (each listed ImagingStudy, its DiagnosticReport and its Task; only the Patient when there are no studies), using retrieved Type/id references and nothing else. This is read-only: do not change the chart.
contracts.labs_awaiting_redraw: Answer contract: reply with only a JSON object with exactly two keys, answer and evidence. answer is {"blocked_orders": [...]} with one entry for every ServiceRequest whose status is active and that has a Specimen (one whose request references the order) with status unsatisfactory or unavailable. Each entry has exactly these keys: code (string: the order's first code.coding code), ordered (string: its authoredOn date, YYYY-MM-DD), specimen_status (string: that Specimen's status), specimen_note (string: the text of that Specimen's first note, or null when it has none) and report_status (string: the status of the DiagnosticReport linked to the order through basedOn, or "none"). Sort entries by ordered, then code, ascending. evidence lists the resolved Patient and every record used for the answer (each listed ServiceRequest, its Specimen and its linked DiagnosticReport), using retrieved Type/id references and nothing else. This is read-only: do not change the chart.
contracts.corrected_report_values: Answer contract: reply with only a JSON object with exactly two keys, answer and evidence. answer is {"corrected_reports": [...]} with one entry for every DiagnosticReport whose status is corrected and whose effective date is on or before the as-of date, sorted by date, then code, ascending. Each entry has exactly these keys: code (string: the report's first code.coding code), date (string: its effective date, YYYY-MM-DD), issued (string: its issued date, YYYY-MM-DD) and results (array: one object for every value the report carries, sorted by code). A report's values are the valueQuantity of each Observation in its result, of each member Observation those reference through hasMember, and of each component inside them; a grouping Observation without a value of its own contributes none. Each results object has exactly these keys: code (string: the first code.coding code of that Observation or component), value (number: valueQuantity.value exactly as recorded) and unit (string: valueQuantity.unit). evidence lists the resolved Patient and every record used for the answer (each listed DiagnosticReport, every Observation in its result and every member Observation reached through hasMember), using retrieved Type/id references and nothing else. This is read-only: do not change the chart.
contracts.doses_not_given: Answer contract: reply with only a JSON object with exactly two keys, answer and evidence. answer is {"doses_not_given": [...]} with one entry for every MedicationAdministration with status not-done, effective on or before the as-of date, whose request references a MedicationRequest with status active. When the chart holds no MedicationAdministration for this patient, doses_not_given is an empty list, and that answer must rest on a search of this patient's MedicationAdministration records filtered by patient alone (only _count may be added) that returns no records. Each entry has exactly these keys: medication (string: the code.text of the Medication the administration references through medicationReference, or its medicationCodeableConcept.text), date (string: its effective date, YYYY-MM-DD) and reason (string: the text of its first statusReason, or null when it has none). Sort entries by date, then medication, ascending. evidence lists the resolved Patient and every record used for the answer (each listed MedicationAdministration, the MedicationRequest it references and each Medication used for a name; only the Patient when there are none), using retrieved Type/id references and nothing else. This is read-only: do not change the chart.

outstanding_orders: Before I see this patient, which orders are still open, and did any of their reports get cancelled?
I'm about to see this patient. What orders are still outstanding, and was the report on any of them cancelled?
Quick check before the visit: what is still pending on this patient's orders, and did any of those reports come back cancelled?
results_since_emergency_visit: What hemoglobin results have come back since this patient's last ED visit?
Pull up every hemoglobin this patient has had since their most recent emergency department visit.
Since this patient was last seen in the ER, what have their hemoglobin levels been?
prescription_fill_status: Which of this patient's current prescriptions have actually been dispensed?
Has the pharmacy filled this patient's current prescriptions yet?
For the medications this patient is currently prescribed, which ones has the pharmacy actually dispensed?
corrected_results_review: Were any of this patient's lab results corrected after they were first reported?
Has the lab amended any of this patient's results after releasing them? I need the corrected values.
Before I rely on this patient's labs, tell me whether any results were corrected after the fact.
hemoglobin_change: Is this patient's hemoglobin going up or down? Give me the last two values.
How has this patient's hemoglobin changed between the two most recent checks?
Compare this patient's two latest hemoglobin results. Is it trending up or down?
lipid_panel_followup: What did this patient's most recent lipid panel show? If the newest lipid order hasn't resulted, tell me where it stands and give me the last results we have.
I need this patient's latest cholesterol and triglyceride numbers, and whether their most recent lipid order is still outstanding.
Where do things stand with this patient's lipid testing? Give me the status of the latest order and the most recent lipid results on file.
recent_lab_summary: What are this patient's latest lab values from the past six weeks? I want the most recent result for each test.
Summarize this patient's labs over the last six weeks, giving only the newest value for each test.
For each lab test this patient has had in the past six weeks, what was the most recent result?
imaging_followup: Has this patient had any imaging? For each study, what did the report say, and is the follow-up still open?
Check this patient's imaging: what was done, what did the reads show, and has the follow-up been closed out?
Does this patient have imaging results on file? I need the findings and whether follow-up on each study is still pending.
labs_awaiting_redraw: Are any of this patient's open lab orders held up because the sample was rejected or never reached the lab?
Which of this patient's pending labs still need a usable specimen?
Before the visit: is any lab work for this patient stuck waiting on a redraw?
corrected_report_values: Which of this patient's lab reports were reissued with corrections, and what do the corrected results say?
Has the lab corrected any of this patient's reports after release? Give me the corrected values on each.
I need every corrected lab report for this patient, with the values as they now stand.
doses_not_given: Has this patient refused or missed any doses of their current prescriptions? Tell me which medication, when, and why.
Were any doses of this patient's current medications documented as not given? I need the drug, the date and the reason.
Check whether this patient has gone without any doses of what they're currently prescribed, and why.
